Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. Ankush Singhal, Advocate for
the petitioners.
2. Mr. K.N. Joshi, Deputy Advocate
General and Mr. Dinesh Bankoti, Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, Advocate
for respondent nos. 2 & 3.
4. Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the
UPNL/respondent no. 4.
5. Since common questions of law
and fact are involved in these
petitions, therefore, they are being
heard and decided together. However,
for the sake of brevity and
convenience, facts of WPSS No. 464 of
2025 alone are being considered and
discussed.
6. Petitioners were engaged
thorough outsourcing agency for
discharging duties as Junior Engineer
in Jal Jeevan Mission, which was
implemented by Uttarakhand Jal
Sansthan. According to the
petitioners, they were initially
engaged for a period of about three

2026:UHC:2564
years till 31.03.2025, and upon expiry
of that term, their engagement was
not extended any further.
7. By means of this writ petition,
petitioners have sought the following
reliefs:-
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing & commanding
the respondents to extend the services of the
petitioner on the post of Junior Engineer as the
petitioners are working for more than last 2-3
years in the said post in the respondent
department without any break, as the Jal
Jeevan Mission for which the petitioners were
appointed is extended till the year 2028.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of Mandamus directing the respondents
restrain respondents from terminating the
services of the petitioners from the said post in
question and also to permit them to continue on
the posts held by them i.e. Junior Engineer.
iii. Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the order dated
10/03/2025 issued by respondent No-3
(Annexure No.2)
iv. Issue writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the respondent
authority to grant the salary to the petitioners
which have not been granted since more than 6
months."
8. Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, learned
counsel appearing for Uttarakhand Jal
Sansthan submits that as many as
288 regular Junior Engineers were
appointed in the year 2025 and after
such regular appointment, there is no
vacancy left against which petitioners
can be engaged. He further submits
that petitioners were engaged through
outsourcing and an outsourced
employee has no lien on the post nor
he can claim any right for

2026:UHC:2564
re-engagement, upon expiry of the
term.
9. This Court finds substance in the
submission made by learned counsel
appearing for the Jal Sansthan.
10. Since all the posts of Junior
Engineers in Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan
have been filled by regular
appointment, therefore there cannot
be any direction for re-engaging the
petitioners on contract through
outsourcing agency.
11. Learned counsel for the
petitioners then submits that the Jal
Jeevan Mission is a centrally funded
scheme, which is likely to continue till
2028 and services of Junior Engineers
are needed in that scheme, therefore,
the respondents be directed to
consider petitioners' claim for
engagement against vacancies
available in the scheme.
12. The writ petitions are,
accordingly, disposed of by permitting
the petitioners to make
representation(s) to the competent
authority. If petitioners make
representation(s) within two weeks,
the competent authority shall take
decision thereupon, as per law, within
two months thereafter.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 09.04.2026
Navin
